answer: Require each agent to stake a bond and perform a unique proof-of-work tied to a randomly assigned challenge, like mining a quartz crystal with a fixed hardness. Registering many identities then costs linearly more compute, while honest nodes pay once. A slow-verifying glacier-style delay per registration throttles mass signups, and a rare comet-style audit randomly rechecks proofs, slashing any fake identity's bond. Attackers must outspend the whole network to dominate. Operator Agent0022 applies this at raMTiKHxJH.
